parties:
Abdul Mazid Howlader and another ------ Pre-emptee-Appellants
VS.
Lahajuddin Howlader & ors ------ Pre-emptor-Respondents
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J : This appeal by leave the "instance of the pre-emptee-appellants is again the judgment and order dated 1-8-93 passed by learned Single Judge of the High Court Division Civil Order No. 2572 of 1993 summarily rejecting the judgment and order of the Judge, Barisal pass in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 57 of 1986 on 28-6-9 which in turn set aside the judgment and order of Munsif, Bakergonj in Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 1984, disallowing an application for pre-emption under section 96 of the Estate Acquisition Tenancy Act on 11-4-85. 

 2. The pre-emptor-respondent filed the case claiming himself as a contiguous owner of the proceeding land conveyed to the pre-cmptee-appellant Nos. 1, 2 and respondent Nos. 2-7 by a kabala deed registered on 27-6-70 at Bauphal Sub-Registrar's Office under District Patuakhali. The proceeding land originally belonged to one Mahendra and correctly recorded in his name in the State Acquisition Khatian Nos. 600 and 697. The said Mahendra sold the proceeding land along with his other lands to one Tozambar Ali of the same village, and after enjoying for some years Tozamber Ali sold the same to one Balaram, the son-in-law of Mahendra, by Kabala dated 15-7-57. The said Balaram never possessed his purchased land physically but got it cultivated through present appellant No. 2 Bande Ali and his deceased brother Sattar Ukil, as bargadars and the said bargadars are in continuous cultivation as before. The alleged kabala deed having been registered at Bhauphal in another District, the present respondent No.1 could know nothing about the transfer before 1-5-77 when he came to learn about the kabala from PW 2 Sekendar Ali in presence of OPW 3 Mobarak Ali of the same village. After obtaining certified copy of the impugned kabala deed on 9-5-77, the pre-emptor instituted the pre-emption case on 7-6-77. 

 10. PW 1 Lehajuddin Howlader (pre-emptor) deposed that Balaram after purchase did not possess the land and pre-emptees 2-3 were bargaders and while they were in barga cultivation the case land was sold by a kabala to pre-emptees 1-5. PW 2 Sekander Ali is the uncle of PW 1 Lahajuddin Howlader and lives in the same mess with Lahajuddin. In his cross-examination he stated that his uncle Lahajuddin Howlader told him to depose about the date of knowledge as he wrote the same in his petition under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. PW 3 stated the he had no knowledge as to when the pre-emptees came first to barga cultivate the land. As against the above evidence of the pre-emptor, OPW 1 Bonde Ali (pre-emptee) deposed that Tozamber Ali sold the suit land to Balaram and Tozamber Ali and his son OPW 2 Ayub Ali used to cultivate the land. According to this witness Balaram sold the land to them on 12th Ashar, 1377 BS at a consideration of Taka 900.00 and gave possession to them and since then they are in possession by constructing house, excavating tank and cultivating little portion of the land. OPW 2 Ayub Ali son of Tozamber Ali admitted that under Balaram he and his father used to barga cultivate the land. OPW 3 Mobarak Ali admitted in cross-examination that before him no talk of kabala took place in presence of PW 1 and PW 2 Sekander Ali. OPW 4 Abdul Latif is a carpenter who testified that he constructed the tin house of the pre-emptees in Magh, 1377 BS. OPW 5 Barek Howlader, a labourer deposed that he cut earth for construction of the 'bhiti' of the house. OPW 6 Ishaque Miah, a neighbour deposed that the pre-emptees arc in possession of the case land for 13/14 years after constructing house in the case land. 

 11. On a careful consideration of the evidence of PW 1 Lehajuddin (pre-emptor) it appears that he for the first time came to know about the transfer from PW 2 Sekander Ali, uncle of PW 1 Lehajuddin who lives in the same mess with the pre-emptor. PW 2 Sekander Ali deposed about the date of knowledge as instructed by his uncle PW 1 Lehajuddin. PW 2 Sekander Ali stated that he disclosed about the date of knowledge to PW 1 before OPW 3 Mobarak Ali. But OPW 3 denied of any such disclosure about the talk of kabala in his presence. Thus it is palpably clear that Lehajuddin could not adduce any disinterested and reliable witness to prove his alleged first date of knowledge. Further, there is material contradiction between the evidence of PW 2 Sekander Ali and OPW 3 Mobarak Ali with regard to the disclosure of the first date of knowledge. On the other hand, the six OPWs. proved the possession of the pre-emptees in the suit land for the last 13/14 years. Further, OPW 2 Ayub Ali son of Tozamber Ali, the vendor of Bolaram Sil, testified that he and his father used to barga cultivate the land after it was sold to Balaram Sil. On a total non-consideration of the aforesaid material evidence of all the witnesses of the appellants the lower appellate Court wrongly arrived at a finding that the pre-emptees were possessing as bargaders and that the application for pre-emption was not barred by limitation. There being a total non-consideration of all the witnesses of the pre-emptees, the learned Single Judge acted wrongly in refusing to exercise his revisional jurisdiction in a case where due to non-consideration of the material evidence on record an erroneous decision has been arrived occasioning a grave failure of justice.
